names_for.custom_side: Request Artefact (a link on the dataset page; what happens after a request is not documented; AIKosh does no collection to order)

operator_role.note: Government-run host: contributors keep IP, set the end-use licence and approve restricted downloads; AIKosh takes only a non-exclusive hosting licence.

economics_model.note: No dataset fee, price or payment mechanism appears in the terms, FAQ or manual; the platform is funded under the IndiaAI Mission.

who_pays_fee.note: No fees are charged to contributors or downloaders in any document found.

supply_models.note: Ministries and registered institutions upload their own data; contributors also relist public Kaggle, Hugging Face and research datasets such as Flickr30k. No evidence of AIKosh collecting its own datasets.

custody_model.note: Uploaded files are hosted by AIKosh; Kaggle imports are redirect links; the API route leaves data with the contributor while downloads pass through AIKosh.

transaction_mode.note: Open datasets download after login; restricted ones after the contributor approves a reasoned request. Nothing is sold.

public_prices.note: No dataset is priced; the only published figures are free compute tiers (c042).

licence_model.note: Contributor picks from a dropdown of standard licences (CC, ODC, Open Government License India, Other, NA) or carries its own, e.g. ICAR Data Use License.

public_listing.note: Live detail pages were readable anonymously and are listed in the public sitemap; the user manual says detail view needs login (see conflicts). Download needs login.

buyer_vetting.note: Platform check is a login via MeriPehchaan/Entity Locker; for restricted datasets the contributor vets each requester case by case.

sample_mechanics.note: Tabular snippet plus column-level statistics on the dataset page.

versioning.note: File edits create a new version and downloads are addressed by version number; whether old versions stay downloadable is not stated.

human_subject_consent_docs.note: Platform policy is non-personal, anonymised data only; no consent or release evidence is shown to downloaders, and masking is left to contributors.

contributor_pay_model.note: Contributors grant a royalty-free licence and nothing is sold, so no one is paid per download.

catalogue_plus_custom.note: AIKosh only lists ready-made datasets; the Request Artefact link is the only gesture toward demand-led supply and its handling is undocumented.

erasure_after_sale.note: Artefacts can be deleted or removed from AIKosh, but content is meant to stay under its licence once downloaded; no downloader deletion duty found.

quality_evidence.note: Org admin and platform admin approve each upload and the platform computes a quality score; descriptions and metadata are the contributor's; terms disclaim accuracy.

Q1.answer: IndiaAI says AIKosh had over 25,000 registrations and pitches datasets to public and private sectors building AI applications; no data on who downloads photo or video, in what volume, or why.

Q2.answer: The EOI pitches contributors on reach to public and private AI builders, community cleaning, versioning, and running challenges and hackathons on their data; there is no revenue motive because nothing is sold.

Q3.answer: Supply is ministries, departments and registered institutions (individuals barred), plus relisted public Kaggle, Hugging Face and research datasets; each is listed under the contributor's chosen licence with AIKosh holding only a non-exclusive hosting licence.

Q4.answer: AIKosh hosts free contributions; there is no commissioned work and no resale, so no carve-out or after-the-fact term change was found.

Q5.answer: AIKosh is a government-run venue: the contributor keeps IP and is licensor under its chosen licence, represents it has rights to the content, and indemnifies AIKosh; AIKosh disclaims all warranties including licence compliance.

Q6.answer: Mixed: uploads are hosted on AIKosh and downloaded by file or version via UI or API; Kaggle imports are redirect links; an API route leaves the data on the contributor's systems.

Q7.answer: Only non-personal, anonymised data is meant to be contributed, in line with DPDPA; responsibility for masking sits with the contributor; no consent from people depicted is documented to downloaders, even on a photo dataset.

Q8.answer: The contributor's chosen licence is meant to travel with the data after download; AIKosh shares downloader identity and usage with contributors and contributors can revoke restricted access; no audit, fingerprinting or exclusivity terms were found.

Q9.answer: No purchase: open datasets download after login; restricted ones need a reasoned request the contributor approves, with appeal after 5 days and escalation to support after 10; no fees or commission.

Q10.answer: A dataset is an artefact with metadata, access level and numbered versions; file edits create a new version; contributors can request deletion subject to admin approval; what past downloaders get on a new version or withdrawal is not stated.

Q11.answer: Before download a user sees metadata, a tabular sample preview, column statistics and a platform-computed Data Quality / AI Readiness score; uploads are approved by organisation and platform admins, though the terms disclaim accuracy.

Q12.answer: AIKosh is catalogue-only (Datasets Repository); a 'Request Artefact' link invites requests for missing data but its handling is undocumented and AIKosh does not collect to order.

conflicts.resolution: The manual says detail views need login, but live detail pages were readable anonymously on 2026-10-01; public_listing follows the live pages.
The terms say AIKosh does not actively pre-screen content, while the FAQ says every upload needs organisation-admin and platform-admin approval before it is visible; both are live.

Different undated counts (over 10,000 datasets from 55+ entities vs 15999+ datasets and 671 organisations on the live home page); likely different dates and measures, not reconcilable from the sources.

leads.why: PIB press releases on the 6 March 2025 launch and later AIKosh milestones; WebFetch got 403 and no search was available to find release IDs.
Security-measures document found in the site's JS bundle; not read.
Privacy policy; may say more on sharing downloader data with contributors.
Competitions with prize pools; relevant to how contributors are rewarded without sales.
